dimensions.assessment: Affects federal land managers and individuals or businesses interested in leasing hardrock minerals on federally acquired lands.
dimensions.evidence: federal lands may be leased for mining hardrock minerals only if the federal lands were acquired under a statute

dimensions.assessment: Changes the legal eligibility of acquired lands for hardrock mineral leasing, potentially altering mining access.
dimensions.evidence: This bill specifies that all federally acquired lands are eligible to be considered for hardrock mineral leasing

dimensions.assessment: The source does not provide specific figures on federal spending or revenue changes.
Amends the Mineral Leasing Act for Acquired Lands to include hardrock minerals alongside existing listed resources.
dimensions.evidence: The Mineral Leasing Act for Acquired Lands (30 U.S.C. 351 et seq.) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change affecting national federal lands.

missing_information: Specific data on the acreage or economic value of newly eligible acquired lands.
Expected changes in federal leasing revenues or administrative costs.
importance_detail.rationale: This bill expands hardrock mineral leasing eligibility to all federally acquired lands under the Mineral Leasing Act for Acquired Lands, affecting federal land management and potential mining interests.
